name: due-work-harness
description: Test Python background jobs for lost tasks, duplicate processing, and missing effects after crashes, retries, or database commits.

interface.longDescription: Does a Celery task disappear after a Django database commit? Can a retry charge a customer twice, resend an email, or process a Kafka message again after an offset-commit failure? Due Work Harness helps a coding agent trace the real workflow, write pytest crash-and-retry histories, and check whether orders, payments, receipts, notifications, imports, and other effects are lost or repeated. It is useful for database-to-queue handoffs, transactional outboxes, worker crashes, redelivery, uncertain API replies, and idempotency checks. The package has specific adapters for Django, Celery, MongoDB, Redis/RQ, Prefect, and aiokafka, plus a framework-free Python core; each adapter covers particular boundaries, not every feature of that system. Proofs run in a coding environment with the target repository and appropriate test services, not through a hosted MCP server.
defaultPrompt: Can this Celery task get lost after the Django transaction commits?
Could a retry charge twice or send a duplicate receipt?
Test whether this Kafka consumer repeats work after a crash.
